title: What training do home health aides need under 42 CFR 484.80?
description: Home health aide rules under 42 CFR 484.80: 75 training hours, the competency evaluation, 12 hours of yearly in-service and RN supervision, at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Under 42 CFR 484.80, a home health aide working for a Medicare-certified home health agency must complete at least 75 hours of classroom and supervised practical training, including at least 16 classroom hours before 16 supervised practical hours, and pass a competency evaluation performed by a registered nurse. After that, each aide needs at least 12 hours of in-service training in every 12-month period. A 24-month gap in paid aide work restarts the requirement.
keyTakeaways: Four routes qualify an aide: the agency's training plus competency evaluation, a competency evaluation alone, a state-approved nurse aide program with good standing on the state registry, or a state licensure program meeting 484.80(b) and (c).
Training totals at least 75 hours. At least 16 classroom hours must come before at least 16 hours of supervised practical training, and the program must cover 14 listed subject areas.
Five subject areas, including communication, vital signs, personal care, transfers and range of motion, must be evaluated by observing the aide with a patient or pseudo-patient.
Each aide needs at least 12 hours of in-service training in each 12-month period, supervised by a registered nurse.
An agency that was cited for certain deficiencies, sanctions or penalties in the previous 2 years cannot run its own aide training or competency evaluation program.
regulator: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), US Department of Health and Human Services
appliesTo: Home health agencies (HHAs) participating in Medicare and Medicaid
Individuals furnishing home health aide services for an HHA, including aides provided under arrangement
Organizations offering home health aide training and competency evaluation programs

sections.heading: Who counts as a qualified home health aide?

blocks.text: A qualified home health aide is someone who has completed one of four programs listed in [42 CFR 484.80(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-484/subpart-B/section-484.80). All home health aide services furnished by a Medicare-certified home health agency (HHA) must be provided by a person who meets this standard.

items: A training and competency evaluation program meeting 484.80(b) and (c).
A competency evaluation program meeting 484.80(c) only, for aides who already have the skills.
A state-approved nurse aide training and competency evaluation program under 42 CFR 483.151 to 483.154, with the person currently listed in good standing on the state nurse aide registry.
A state licensure program that meets 484.80(b) and (c).

blocks.text: Qualification lapses. If, since last completing a program, the person has gone 24 consecutive months without furnishing covered aide services for compensation, they must complete another qualifying program before working as an aide again. Hiring checks should therefore record both the program completion date and recent paid aide work. This page states the federal floor as at November 2026, from eCFR text current to November 5, 2026; many states add their own aide rules.

sections.heading: How many hours of training does a home health aide need, and what must it cover?

blocks.text: Classroom and supervised practical training must total at least 75 hours. Within that, a minimum of 16 hours of classroom training must come before a minimum of 16 hours of supervised practical training, which is delivered in a practicum laboratory or other setting under the direct supervision of a registered nurse, or a licensed practical nurse supervised by a registered nurse.

Under 484.80(b)(3), the program must address communication skills (including reading, writing and verbally reporting clinical information); observation, reporting and documentation; temperature, pulse and respiration; basic infection prevention and control; body functioning and reportable changes; a clean, safe and healthy environment; recognizing emergencies and emergency procedures; the needs of the populations the agency serves, including respect for privacy and property; personal hygiene and grooming tasks; safe transfers and ambulation; normal range of motion and positioning; nutrition and fluid intake; recognizing and reporting changes in skin condition; and any other task the agency chooses to have aides perform as permitted under state law.

The personal hygiene checklist names bed bath; sponge, tub and shower bath; hair shampooing in sink, tub and bed; nail and skin care; oral hygiene; and toileting and elimination. The agency must train aides as needed for skills beyond that checklist. Classroom and practical training must be given by a registered nurse with at least 2 years of nursing experience, at least 1 year of it in home health care, or by others under that nurse's general supervision.

sections.heading: How is a home health aide's competency evaluated?

blocks.text: No one may furnish home health aide services until they pass a competency evaluation covering every subject in 484.80(b)(3). A registered nurse performs the evaluation, in consultation with other skilled professionals as appropriate.

blocks.title: 42 CFR 484.80(c)(1): observed subjects
blocks.text: "Subject areas specified under paragraphs (b)(3)(i), (iii), (ix), (x), and (xi) of this section must be evaluated by observing an aide's performance of the task with a patient or pseudo-patient."

Those five are communication skills, vital signs, personal hygiene and grooming, safe transfers and ambulation, and range of motion and positioning. The other subjects may be assessed by written or oral examination, or by observation in a simulation. An aide is not competent in any task rated unsatisfactory and may not perform it without direct registered nurse supervision until retrained and successfully reevaluated. An aide with unsatisfactory ratings in more than one required area has not passed. For assessment design principles, see [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: What ongoing training and supervision do home health aides need?

blocks.text: Each aide must receive at least 12 hours of in-service training during each 12-month period. In-service training may happen while the aide is caring for a patient, may be offered by any organization, and must be supervised by a registered nurse. The agency must keep documentation showing the standard is met.

Supervision visits under 484.80(h) act as an ongoing competency check, and the interval depends on the patient's services. For patients also receiving skilled nursing or therapy, a registered nurse or other skilled professional must complete a supervisory assessment at least every 14 days, in person or, rarely, by two-way audio-video, limited to one virtual assessment per patient in a 60-day episode. An annual on-site visit to observe each aide performing care is also required. For patients receiving aide services only, a registered nurse must visit in person every 60 days and observe each aide on site semiannually.

If a deficiency in aide services is verified on site, the agency must conduct, and the aide must complete, retraining and a competency evaluation for the deficient skill and all related skills. This makes supervision findings a direct trigger for targeted retraining, which a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) should record against the specific skill.

sections.heading: Which organizations may run home health aide training programs?

blocks.text: Any organization may offer aide training and competency evaluation programs, except an HHA that, within the previous 2 years, fell into one of the disqualifying categories in 484.80(f). These include being out of compliance with the training, competency, in-service or instructor standards; letting an unqualified person furnish aide services; an extended survey for substandard care; a civil monetary penalty of $5,000 or more as an intermediate sanction; temporary management; or suspension of Medicare payments.

Agencies in that position must send aides to an outside program. Agencies that use aides under arrangement remain responsible under 484.80(h)(5) for ensuring those aides have met the training or competency evaluation requirements.

sections.heading: How can an agency map 484.80 to records a surveyor will check?

blocks.text: Each standard in 484.80 ends with a duty to keep documentation, so the practical test is whether the agency can produce the record for any named aide. The table below is an illustrative register. HHA staff also need emergency preparedness training at hire and at least every 2 years under [42 CFR 484.102(d)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-484/subpart-C/section-484.102), which is included for completeness.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each 484.80 subject area to learning outcomes and to the assessment method the rule allows, observed or written, so an agency can show that every required area was evaluated in the right way. Supervisory findings can be linked back to the skill and its related skills, which supports the retraining duty. See how this works for [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can a certified nursing assistant work as a home health aide without more training?
faqs.a: Often yes. 484.80(a)(1)(iii) accepts completion of a state-approved nurse aide training and competency evaluation program under 42 CFR 483.151 to 483.154, provided the person is currently listed in good standing on the state nurse aide registry. The 24-month lapse rule still applies, and state law may add requirements.

faqs.q: Can in-service hours be completed online?
faqs.a: The federal rule does not prohibit it. 484.80(d) requires at least 12 hours in each 12-month period, allows any organization to offer the training, and requires registered nurse supervision. Agencies using online modules should be able to show how the nurse supervised the training and should check any state rules on format.

faqs.q: What happens if an aide fails one area of the competency evaluation?
faqs.a: The aide is not considered competent in that task and must not perform it without direct supervision by a registered nurse until retrained and successfully reevaluated. An unsatisfactory rating in more than one required area means the aide has not passed the evaluation at all.

faqs.q: Does the 75 hours have to be done by the employing agency?
faqs.a: No. Any eligible organization may offer the training and competency evaluation programs. The employing agency must still verify the aide's qualification and keep documentation, and an agency barred under 484.80(f) cannot run its own program during the 2-year period.

factCheck.claim: 484.80(a): four qualification routes; (a)(2) 24 consecutive months without compensated services requires a new program. eCFR current to 2026-11-05; last amended 86 FR 62421, Nov. 9, 2021.
484.80(b)(1)-(3): at least 75 hours; minimum 16 classroom hours before minimum 16 supervised practical hours; 14 subject areas plus agency-specific tasks; documentation (b)(4).
484.80(c): competency evaluation before furnishing services; (b)(3)(i), (iii), (ix), (x), (xi) evaluated by observation with patient or pseudo-patient; RN performs; unsatisfactory rules.
484.80(d): at least 12 hours in-service per 12-month period, RN supervised; (e) instructor RN with 2 years nursing experience, 1 in home health care.

484.80(f): HHA barred from offering programs for 2 years after listed events including CMP of $5,000 or more; (h) 14-day supervisory assessment, max 1 virtual per patient per 60-day episode, annual on-site observation; 60-day RN visit and semiannual observation for aide-only patients; retraining and competency evaluation after verified deficiency.
484.102(d)(1): initial emergency preparedness training for new and existing staff, under arrangement and volunteers; at least every 2 years; documentation; training after significant updates.
